title: The CEO Who Paid a Hitman to Kill His Own Company's Whistleblower
hook: When a corporate audit uncovered a $200 million fraud, the CEO didn't fire the accountant—he hired a contract killer.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines true crime with corporate horror—viewers are obsessed with stories where executives cross the line into literal murder.

title: The Startup That Sold 'Miracle Water'—It Was Tap Water with a $200 Price Tag
hook: They raised $45 million from investors who never tested the product, because the 'bottling plant' was a garden hose.
why_this_can_go_viral: Theranos-level audacity but with something as simple as water—makes people furious and fascinated.

title: The Monopoly That Patent-Trolled Every Bakery—Then Made Bread Illegal to Bake at Home
hook: They owned the rights to 'yeast activation in residential ovens' and sued anyone who baked a loaf.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone bakes or eats bread—the idea that a company could legally ban home baking is rage-bait gold.

title: The Corporate Spy Who Stole a Billion-Dollar Formula by Attending a Funeral
hook: He posed as a grieving cousin, walked into the dead chemist's house, and walked out with the secret recipe on a USB drive.
why_this_can_go_viral: Blends death, deception, and high-stakes theft—feels like a spy thriller but it's real.

title: The Dark Marketing Firm That Used Suicide Hotline Calls to Sell Life Insurance
hook: They bought call data from a crisis center and targeted the most vulnerable people with high-premium policies.
why_this_can_go_viral: Morally repugnant and deeply shocking—people will share it out of outrage and disbelief.

title: The CEO Who Fired 200 Employees—Then Hired Them Back as Contractors at Half Pay
hook: He used a legal loophole to eliminate benefits, pensions, and overtime—while sitting on a $50 million bonus.
why_this_can_go_viral: Relatable rage for anyone who's been laid off—shows how easily CEOs can legally destroy lives.

title: The Startup That Sold 'Brain-Computer Interfaces'—They Were Just Tin Foil Hats with LEDs
hook: Investors paid $10,000 each for 'neuro-enhancement' headsets that were literally no different from a potato battery.
why_this_can_go_viral: Absurdly hilarious and infuriating—people love seeing how dumb 'smart money' can really be.

title: The Monopoly That Controlled Every Coffin Supplier—Then Charged $8,000 for a Cardboard Box
hook: They bought up 90% of casket manufacturers, then lobbied to ban 'DIY' burials so you had to buy from them.
why_this_can_go_viral: Death is universal—the idea that a cartel controls how we bury our loved ones is gut-wrenching.

title: The Corporate Spy Who Posed as a Journalist for 3 Years—Then Sold the Interview Recordings
hook: He got a press badge, attended competitor press conferences, and sold every trade secret he heard to the highest bidder.
why_this_can_go_viral: Taps into distrust of media—shows how the press badge can be a weapon for corporate theft.

title: The Dark Marketing Firm That Used Doctor's Office Wi-Fi to Sell Opioid Alternatives
hook: They injected ads into waiting room networks, targeting chronic pain patients with 'natural' supplements that were unregulated drugs.
why_this_can_go_viral: Vulnerable patients being exploited in a medical setting—deeply unethical and shareable.

title: The Supply Chain Secret of 'Fresh' Orange Juice—It Was 18 Months Old and Chemically Debittered
hook: The 'fresh' juice in your fridge is stored in million-gallon tanks and stripped of flavor, then re-flavored with chemical packs.
why_this_can_go_viral: Breaks a beloved breakfast illusion—people feel duped and want to share the disgusting truth.

title: The Industry Cover-Up of 'Safe' Asbestos Removal—Workers Were Told to Use Dust Masks
hook: The company knew the fibers were lethal, but sold 'certified' removal kits that did nothing—hundreds died.
why_this_can_go_viral: Corporate negligence that literally kills—outrage and tragedy drive massive engagement.

title: The CEO Who Ran a 'Zero Emissions' Factory—That Had a Secret Coal Plant in the Basement
hook: He collected $200 million in green subsidies while burning coal 24/7 in an underground room no inspector ever found.
why_this_can_go_viral: Perfect storm of greenwashing hypocrisy—environmentalists and skeptics will both share it.

title: The Startup That Claimed to 'Sequence Your DNA'—It Just Guessed Based on Your Last Name
hook: They charged $500 for a 'personalized genome report' that was actually a spreadsheet of stereotypes linked to your ethnicity.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone who took a DNA test will feel conned—highly shareable identity-based outrage.

title: The Monopoly That Made Every Dentist Use the Same X-Ray Machine—Then Charged $500 Per Scan
hook: They bought every dental imaging patent, then leased the machines for $1/month—but charged a fortune per X-ray.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone hates the dentist and expensive bills—this explains exactly why.

title: The Corporate Spy Who Faked a Suicide to Escape with Stolen Trade Secrets
hook: He left a fake note, a bloody shirt, and a boat full of his belongings—then flew to a non-extradition country with 20,000 files.
why_this_can_go_viral: Feels like a Hollywood heist movie—viewers are glued to the audacity and execution.

title: The CEO Who Bought a Remote Island—Then Made It a Corporate Tax Haven for His Own Company
hook: He declared the island a sovereign nation, named himself 'Minister of Finance,' and paid 0% tax on $2 billion in profit.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines wealth fantasy with legal loophole abuse—viewers are fascinated by how far the rich can push the system.
